 Rain and storms to haunt millions of Halloween trick-or-treaters across 20+ states
 Multiple storm systems are developing over the West, the Lower Mississippi and Tennessee River valleys and the Southeast, leaving only the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast and parts of the Plains and Upper Midwest with a clear and dry trick-or-treating forecast.
 By
 Hayley Vawter , Julian Atienza 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 02:38 Wicked weather to wash out Halloween across Southwest and Southeast 
 Trick-or-treaters could be facing a washout tonight across parts of California, the Southwest, the Deep South, as well as the Gulf Coast and Florida.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 More than 20 states will see periods of rain on Halloween.
 The Southwest and Southeast could see the heaviest downpours, including several flash flood risks.
 The Northeast will have the best trick-or-treating conditions, with clear skies and seasonable temperatures.
 The weather will be playing tricks this Halloween , with trick-or-treaters facing storms across more than 20 states, including a washout for parts of California , the Southwest , the Deep South, as well as the Gulf Coast and Florida .
 Multiple storm systems are developing over the West , the Lower Mississippi and Tennessee River valleys and the Southeast , leaving only the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast and parts of the Plains and Upper Midwest with a clear and dry trick-or-treating forecast.
 NATIONAL PARK SERVICE PUTS A SPOOKY TWIST ON HALLOWEEN WITH PUMPKIN CARVING CHALLENGE 
 Halloween night national forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Get the breakdown of the Halloween forecast for each region:
 Northwest
 The Northwest will be cool, with high temperatures in the 50s and post-sunset temperatures in the 40s.
 Light sprinkles will impact the region on-and-off Saturday, particularly over eastern Oregon and Idaho.
 COULD SUPER EL NIÑO INFLUENCE THE POLAR VORTEX TO DO SOMETHING IT'S NEVER DONE BEFORE THIS WINTER? 
 Northwest Halloween night forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Overall, nothing outside normal for the Pacific Northwest this time of year.
 California and Southwest 
 A potent storm slammed the Southwest late Friday, triggering flash flooding across parts of Nevada, including Las Vegas, and Arizona. An even stronger storm will develop over the region through Halloween today, impacting California , as well as Utah, Arizona, western Colorado and western New Mexico.
 "A good soaking of moderate-to-heavy rain will reach southern California by Saturday. Notably, Los Angeles and San Diego have not seen a lot of rain on Halloween," the FOX Forecast Center said.
 Southwest Halloween forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  San Diego has seen only nine Halloweens with measurable rain since 1850, with the most recent being in 1987, according to the Forecast Center.
 Temperatures will be cooler, especially for those in the higher elevations of the Desert Southwest and Four Corners, which could see an even more pronounced autumnal chill.
 A broad Level 1 out of 4 flash flood risk covers the region and Central Arizona, including Phoenix, is in the bull's-eye of a Level 2 flood threat through Halloween night. 
 MAJOR CROSS-COUNTRY STORM TO BLAST OVER 35 STATES WITH FLOODING RAIN, SNOW THROUGH HALLOWEEN & ELECTION DAY 
 Weather will remain unsettled, as rain and thunderstorms are likely across those areas.
 Texas and Southern Plains
 Rain will taper off through the day across the Southern Plains after parts of West Texas saw flash flooding heading into the weekend from the remnants of Vance.
 500-MILES OF CALIFORNIA COAST BATTLE CONTINUED FLOODING FROM KING TIDES, CLOSING PART OF PACIFIC COAST HIGHWAY 
 Southern Plains Halloween forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Halloween night should be dry across much of Texas and Oklahoma, with temperatures dropping into the upper 50s to upper 60s.
 Midwest
 Spotty showers are possible today across parts of Missouri and Illinois, including Chicago.
 Unseasonably warm weather will continue across the Midwest and Ohio Valley into early November, with little sign of a sustained cooldown. 
 Midwest Halloween forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Meanwhile, temperatures are expected to run 10-20 degrees above average across much of the Midwest, with highs in the 70s and lower 80s in areas that typically see temperatures in the 50s this time of year.
 In Indianapolis, there have been 25 days of 70° or greater. The record in the capital city is 27 and if the forecast holds, they will likely break or tie that record on Halloween.
 Group of People walking on illuminated street on Halloween night
 (Onfokus / Getty Images) 
 Northeast and Mid-Atlantic 
 The Northeast and Mid-Atlantic are expected to see the best weather of the weekend, with dry conditions for most of the regions as high pressure keeps the area quiet.
 Northeast Halloween Forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Mild temperatures in the low-to-mid 60s are likely to accompany, creating pleasant trick-or-treating conditions.
 WHY DO LEAVES CHANGE COLOR IN THE FALL? THE SCIENCE BEHIND NATURE’S COLORFUL TRANSFORMATION 
 But nighttime temperatures could drop into the 40s for evening trick-or-treating.
 AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 31: Community members Trick-or-Treat together in the Allandale neighborhood on October 31, 2023 in Austin, Texas. Community members and families came out to celebrate Halloween together. 
 (Brandon Bell / Getty Images) 
 The nice conditions are expected to be short-lived, as a larger storm system and its moisture plume are forecast to move into the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast by Sunday, bringing rain and gusty winds .
 HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER 
 Southeast
 Heavy rain will move into the region through the day, and could significantly impact some outdoor plans, especially closer to the Mississippi Valley and Gulf Coast, including areas like New Orleans .
 Portions of Alabama, Mississippi and West Tennessee will see heavy rain. 
 Southeast rain forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Florida will also be wet, especially across the eastern coastline where the heaviest rain will set up. 
 Rain will linger Halloween night into Sunday, while temperatures across Southeast will be warmer than usual, with highs in the mid to upper 70s.
 Stick with FOX Weather as we bring you the latest forecast across the U.S. heading into Halloween weekend.
